issues.source_quote: Пароль старый - "Чёрт побери!"
issues.translation_quote: Same password: "Damn it!"
issues.justification: The recurring password phrase is rendered inconsistently across the scene ("Damn it" vs. the earlier 'God damn it'), and the humor of the mispronounced password "Щорт побери" is lost because the English doesn't mark the foreign accent.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: May you live... on nothing but... your salary!
issues.justification: The famous curse is weakened; the translation hedges with ellipses and loses the comic punch of a mundane 'curse' (live on one salary), and the preceding curse's Russian dialectal flavor ("у гробу, у белых тапках") is flattened.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Buy a whole ticket pack, win... a tractor rack!
issues.justification: The rhyming lottery slogan is altered to an invented, nonsensical prize; the absurd comic prize (a water tower/pump) is lost.

issues.source_quote: Они, конечно, предложат большой выкуп, а я ещё поторгуюсь.
issues.translation_quote: Of course, they'll offer a big reward, and I'll bargain with them.
issues.justification: 'Выкуп' means ransom (they buy back the goods); 'reward' misrepresents the meaning.

issues.source_quote: за чужой счёт пьют даже трезвенники и язвенники
issues.translation_quote: even teetotalers and convalescers drink
issues.justification: 'Язвенники' means people with ulcers, not 'convalescers'; mistranslation.

issues.source_quote: Если человек идиот - то это надолго.
issues.translation_quote: If a man is an idiot, it's for a long time!
issues.justification: Literal rendering; the boss's aphorism parody sounds awkward and the sardonic delivery is weak; also the first boss aphorism 'главное - реализм' is fine but this one misses idiomatic punch ('being an idiot is for life').

issues.source_quote: Куй железо, не отходя от кассы!
issues.translation_quote: strike while the iron's hot and don't leave the till!
issues.justification: The mashed-up idiom (a pun merging two proverbs) is rendered clumsily; 'don't leave the till' is not a natural English joke and the wit is lost, though recognizable.

issues.source_quote: Такси? Говорит Семён Семёнович Горбунков.
issues.translation_quote: Taxi service? This is Semyon Semyonovich Gorbunkov.
issues.justification: Fine, but the following 'Спасибо' etc. okay; minor: the call is a coded signal to police, which the translation leaves unexplained. Low impact.

issues.source_quote: Островом Невезения ... Видно, в понедельник их мама родила.
issues.translation_quote: Their mothers must have borne them on a Monday night
issues.justification: The song is reworked into rhymes that diverge from the original; 'Им бы понедельники взять и отменить' becomes 'ban that Monday from the line', and 'no calendar' lines are adapted loosely, losing the 'Monday is a hard day' joke and the 'ужасные на лицо, добрые внутри' gist is only partly retained.

issues.source_quote: трынь-траву
issues.translation_quote: don't-care grass
issues.justification: 'Трынь-трава' is an idiom meaning 'nothing matters/no big deal' and also a magical herb; 'don't-care grass' is awkward and the pun with 'Володька Трынкин' is also lost.

issues.source_quote: Нет, нет, нет, нет, нет! А я взял... Водку?
issues.translation_quote: No, no, no, no! Well, I did... Vodka?
issues.justification: Minor omission of one 'no' is trivial but the exchange is slightly off in sequence; the speakers are muddled.

issues.source_quote: Пурген ласт "Чёрт побери"? [Пароль старый - "Чёрт побери!"]
issues.translation_quote: Purgen last "Damn it"?
issues.justification: The invented-language gibberish is transliterated inconsistently with the subtitle glosses and some (e.g. 'Zigel') alter the sound-play; the comic pseudo-foreign effect is only partly retained.

issues.source_quote: Ладыженский, Евгений Николаевич, школьный друг этого дурика!
issues.translation_quote: this silly fellow's school friend!
issues.justification: 'Дурик' is affectionate, colloquial and drunk; 'silly fellow' is too prim for a drunken traveler's speech.

issues.source_quote: Нет, на это я пойтить не могу!
issues.translation_quote: No! I ain't doing no such thing!
issues.justification: Lyolik's substandard 'пойтить' is rendered with heavy American-rural slang ('ain't doing no such thing'), which mismatches the character's voice elsewhere.

issues.source_quote: Без опозданий!
issues.translation_quote: No lateness!
issues.justification: Unnatural; 'No being late' or 'Don't be late' would be idiomatic.

issues.source_quote: Не положено, инструкция! Не взял попутных - это не таксист!
issues.translation_quote: Not allowed. Regulations! He won't take other passengers. He's no taxi driver!
issues.justification: Garbled speaker split; Gorbunkov's inner suspicion about the driver not picking up fares is mangled.

issues.source_quote: Нет, нет, не надо, я сам... Семён Семёнович, ну давайте без самодеятельности!
issues.translation_quote: No, no. I'll pay myself... Semyon Semyonovich, please don't improvise!
issues.justification: 'Without amateur initiative' carries a Soviet institutional flavor; 'improvise' is acceptable but loses the 'amateur theatre' echo with the earlier 'самодеятельность' question.

issues.source_quote: Вы в самодеятельности участвуете?
issues.translation_quote: Do you perform in amateur theater?
issues.justification: Stilted; 'Do you take part in amateur performances?' sounds more natural.

issues.source_quote: Twasn't my fault!
issues.translation_quote: Twasn't my fault!
issues.justification: 'Twasn't' is archaic and mismatches Nadya's modern colloquial voice.

issues.source_quote: Не виноватая я! Он сам пришёл!
issues.translation_quote: Twasn't my fault! He came here on his own!
issues.justification: Register shift: the Russian is a woman's colloquial protest; archaic English misleads.

issues.source_quote: Ясно - собутыльник!
issues.translation_quote: I see. A drinking buddy!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but earlier 'Как у вас там говорят, топай до хазы' is rendered 'get back to your pad', which loses the mocking criminal-slang quote.

issues.source_quote: Игрушки идиотские
issues.translation_quote: Those idiotic toys!
issues.justification: Acceptable; however 'Тлетворное влияние Запада' is rendered adequately.

issues.source_quote: Шампанское по утрам пьют или аристократы, или дегенераты!
issues.translation_quote: In the morning, champagne is drunk only by aristocrats and degenerates.
issues.justification: The punchy Soviet aphorism is rendered as stiff passive prose, and 'только' is added; spoken punch is lost.

issues.source_quote: Такова «сё ля ви», как говорят у них...
issues.translation_quote: Such is "c'est la vie," as they say here...
issues.justification: 'у них' means 'over there' (abroad); 'here' reverses the reference. Also the deliberate mangling of the French is lost.

issues.source_quote: Печёнкой чую, клюнула настоящая рыба.
issues.translation_quote: I can feel it in my gut. We've hooked a real fish.
issues.justification: Fine, but the fishing metaphor of 'клюнула' (she bit) shifts to 'we've hooked'; acceptable. Low impact.

issues.source_quote: Я встретил Вас и всё былое В отжившем сердце ожило...
issues.translation_quote: I met you, and all that was past Awoke in my weary heart...
issues.justification: The romance's stock phrases are rendered adequately, but 'отжившем' (outlived/spent) is softened.

issues.source_quote: Ну-с, начнём, пожалуй!
issues.translation_quote: Well then, let's begin!
issues.justification: Lacks the jovial theatrical flavor, but minor in effect.

issues.source_quote: Ха-га-га-га-га-га-га-га-га-га-га! ... Всё меняется, операцию будем проводить у Белой Скалы...
issues.translation_quote: We'll do it at White Cliff.
issues.justification: 'Скала' is a rock/crag; 'Cliff' is acceptable but inconsistent with 'Black Rocks'.

issues.source_quote: Туалэт, типа сортир, обозначенный на схеме буквами «Мэ» и «Жо»
issues.translation_quote: lavatory, a sort of outhouse, marked on the plan with "M" and "W."
issues.justification: The joke on М/Ж (men/women) letters in Cyrillic is partially retained, but the pronunciation 'Мэ/Жо' (with a hidden crude pun) is lost.

issues.source_quote: Летять уткы… Летять у... утки... и-и два-а гуся-я...
issues.translation_quote: The ducks are flying... The ducks are... flying... and two... geese...
issues.justification: The reference to the well-known song 'Летят утки' is flattened into plain narration; the cultural allusion and the mock-comic effect are lost.
